content:
Ava (Design): quick design check: propose an inline guardrail badge next to the min/max that warns when changes may violate SLO guardrails. mock in figma: https://figma.com/file/xxxxx/guardrail-badge
Jon (PM): love it. Should the badge be passive (info) or a blocking modal? I think passive with an optional confirm is better.
Marta (Frontend): passive badge + confirm on submit sounds good. Implementation: show badge on focus/hover, aria-live announce when it appears.
Leo (A11y): accessibility: badge must be reachable via keyboard, use aria-describedby for the control, and announce the reason: e.g., "Warning: change may increase p99 latency by ~40ms."
Kai (Infra): infra note: calculate guardrail trigger client-side with cached metrics, but verify server-side on commit. debounce API validation to avoid spamming.
Ava (Design): microcopy options: ["Guardrail: may impact SLO", "Warning: potential SLO impact", "Heads up: latency may increase"]. Which reads best?
Jon (PM): prefer "Warning: potential SLO impact". direct but not scary.
Marta (Frontend): will add small tooltip: "Why?" linking to a short explainer modal. also use role="status" for the badge so screenreaders get it immediately.
Leo (A11y): role="status" is good; ensure modal has role="dialog" and focus trap. contrast on badge must meet AA.
Kai (Infra): one more: if users hit confirm after a guardrail, include a server-side audit event so we can track guardrail overrides.
Ava (Design): thanks 44d will update figma and push copy: "Warning: potential SLO impact". planning to prototype this afternoon.
